s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral limb weakness with aphasia and an intracranial lesion
salient_findings: Abnormal CSF analysis with high cell count and protein
Lung mass with pleural invasion on chest CT
key_facts: 66-year-old man
Progressive right-sided limb weakness for 3 days
Excessive smoking history
Thyroid nodules in past medical history
No history of hypertension, diabetes, or heart disease
WBC count 14.53*10^9/L
Neutrophils 79%
Blood glucose 5.82mmol/L
CSF cell count 322*10^6/L
CSF total protein 950 mg/L
Head MRI shows left parietal occupying lesion with severe edema and circular enhancement
Chest CT shows left lung mass with pleural invasion
Lung biopsy shows inflammatory cell infiltrates and fibrin-like exudates
Brain lesion pathology shows multiple fungal hyphae

shortlist.label: Lung cancer with brain metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a lung mass with pleural invasion and a brain lesion with severe edema and circular enhancement, suggesting metastasis

shortlist.label: Intracranial fungal infection
shortlist.why_kept: Brain lesion pathology shows multiple fungal hyphae, and patient has a compromised immune system due to excessive smoking history

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fungal hyphae in brain lesion pathology and patient's history of excessive smoking, which increases risk of aspergillosis

shortlist.label: Cerebral abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated WBC count, neutrophils, and CSF cell count, suggesting an infectious process

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a brain lesion with severe edema and circular enhancement, which could be consistent with a primary brain tumor
